data.title: A lecture on the Celts in south-western Slovakia (video)
data.excerpt: On 5 October 2017 we organised a lecture by Radoslav Čambal and Marek Budaj of the Slovak National Museum on the Celts in south-western Slovakia, which was broadcast live and can still be watched as a recording. The same day at Tvrdošovce visitors could also see a borrowed exhibition on the Celts, finds of the Celtic period and large-format visualisations of a Celtic settlement.

children.text: On 5 October 2017, together with Dwarf Digital Archeology and the Slovak National Museum, we organised a lecture by Radoslav Čambal and Marek Budaj, members of the staff of the Slovak National Museum, on the subject of “The Celts in south-western Slovakia”. We broadcast the whole lecture live and you can also watch the recording at

On Wednesday 5 October 2017 at Tvrdošovce, besides the lecture on the Celts that we streamed online, you could also see an exhibition entitled “The remarkable Celtic people”, which was lent to us by Constantine the Philosopher University in Nitra. Visitors could also look at several borrowed finds of the Celtic period and enjoy large-format prints of Dwarf Digital's visualisations of a Celtic settlement. There was of course also the opportunity to talk in person to the archaeologists Radoslav Čambal, Igor Bazovský and Martin Furman, as well as to the numismatist Marek Budaj.
